newsitem.title: USA: Morgan Stanley's Biggs cuts stocks in portfolio.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Stanley's Biggs cuts stocks in portfolio.

text.p: Morgan Stanley Dean Witter strategist Barton Biggs raised the cash position and reduced stocks in his balanced model portfolio, the firm said on Monday.
Biggs raised cash in the Balanced Financial Asset Portfolio to 15 from 10 percent.

He reduced the portfolio's equity position to 53 from 58 percent. Of the five percent reduction, two percent came out of U.S. equities, one percent out of Europe, Australia and the Far East, and two percent out of emerging markets.
A Morgan Stanley Dean Witter statement did not give details on the remainder of the portfolio and Biggs was not immediately available for comment.

"History shows that the most effective way to trade in and out of this sort of market is to go against extremes of sentiment," the statement said. It listed bullish consensus at "an all-time high" at 80 percent.
"All this could be setting us up for something significant to happen this summer," it added.
It said Japan may be a market that could be "delinked" from the U.S. market and could go up even as other markets around the world went down.

The statement also cited the view that the International Monetary Fund has recommended to Thailand that it change the peg on the baht and perhaps expand the band within which it fluctuates in return for a loan agreement.
"If this were successful, it could be quite buillish for the Thai stock market," the statement said.
Government steps to defend the currency through high short-term rates and financial controls has exacted a high price from the Thai economy in terms of growth and business failures, it said.
